why: Two strings, one used as a subsequence and one as a substring: a 2-D DP over prefixes. dp[i][j] = longest suffix of y[:j] (a substring ending at j) that is a subsequence of x[:i]; it extends diagonally on a match and carries down from the previous x-prefix otherwise.
hints: A substring of y is fixed by where it ends; ask for each end j how long a block ending there can be found in order inside x.
dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1 if x[i-1] == y[j-1] (the block grows by y[j-1] matched to x[i-1]), else dp[i-1][j] (x[i-1] is skipped).
Fill an (|x|+1) x (|y|+1) table row by row keeping only one previous row, answer = maximum entry. O(|x| * |y|) time, O(|y|) space.
pitfalls: This is not LCS: on a mismatch you may not drop a character of y (the y side must stay contiguous), so do not take dp[i][j-1].
And not longest common substring either: x's characters may be skipped.
Take the maximum over the whole table, not dp[|x|][|y|].
